style.masterSentence: Premium AAA mobile puzzle-game illustration: chunky, charming toy-like 3/4 forms, strong simplified silhouettes, smooth glossy enamel, controlled brass accents, warm cream mounting plates, and bold dark-colored outlines. Clean sculpted geometry, restrained highlights, soft dimensional shadows, warm studio lighting, vivid but disciplined colors, instantly readable at thumbnail size, handcrafted polish, never photorealistic.
style.styleLock:
OMM_STYLE_LOCK_V2
Camera: orthographic-like 3/4 view, 30 degrees above the subject, seeing its front and right sides, no wide-angle distortion. Light: from the upper-left, one broad soft highlight and one restrained specular streak per major surface; soft contact shadow falls lower-right. Shapes: chunky rounded geometric forms, exaggerated readable proportions. Outline: dark chocolate or dark local-color, about 4-5 percent of the object's visible width, the same weight everywhere, NEVER pure black.
Palette: vermilion red #E9422B, warm gold #F3B62F, cobalt blue #168DE0, cream #F2E6C9, dark charcoal #303139, brass #C99532. Controlled secondary accents only: emerald #27B957, cyan #35CDEB, violet #9343CB. Surfaces: smooth painted toy enamel, satin brass, warm painted metal, clean ceramic. Brass is an accent material under 20 percent of the surface, never the main body.
Machines always sit on a compact cream beveled mounting plate with four simplified brass corner feet, plate no wider than 115 percent of the machine body. Monsters, icons, UI parts and effects have no plate. Everything is fully visible, centered, with a 10 percent empty margin on every side. Favor silhouette, readability and cohesive handcrafted shapes over extra detail. The smallest detail must survive at 64 pixels.
Exceptions that the asset prompt may state: UI frames are front-facing, not 3/4; backgrounds may have soft atmosphere; effects have no outline and use white or soft color on black.
style.negatives: NO photorealism, realistic PBR rendering, thin outlines, black outlines, sketch lines, painterly brush strokes, gritty textures, rust, scratches, dirt, excessive rivets, excessive gears, microscopic mechanical detail, complex reflections, chrome, raw grey steel, hard reflections, blown highlights, heavy bloom, harsh shadows, flat vector art, stock-vector gradients, pixel art, anime styling, watercolor, neon overload, random colors, mismatched camera angles, perspective distortion, oversized bases, clutter, text, letters, numbers, watermarks, borders, cropped objects, inconsistent proportions, cheap plastic look, generic AI detail noise, real brand or product trade dress.
style.keyColourRule: You cannot make real transparency, so I key the background out myself. Unless the prompt says otherwise, put every object on ONE perfectly flat, uniform, pure magenta background #FF00FF. No gradient, no shadow on the background, no glow outside the outline, no floor, no checkerboard, no white. Any hole inside an object (a shackle, a gear center, a handle loop) must also show flat magenta, never white. Do not use magenta or hot pink inside the object. If a subject has ANY violet, purple, lilac, pink or magenta part (a purple ribbon, a violet gem, a pink heart), use flat pure green #00FF00 as the key instead: the prompt will say "flat green #00FF00 background", and then nothing in the object may be green-screen green. Never put a violet or purple subject on magenta. Effects meant for additive blending are white or soft color on a pure black #000000 background. Full-screen backgrounds and screen mockups have no key.

keyColours.green: #00FF00 REQUIRED when the subject has any violet, purple, lilac, pink or magenta part (CRITIQUE_2: a violet ribbon keyed on magenta leaked 176 key pixels)

deviationsFromGptText: Transparent background is replaced by a flat magenta (or green, or black for additive FX) key, because the critic pass showed white backgrounds leave fringes and white holes (CRITIQUE_1, patterns 2 and 3) and ChatGPT cannot be trusted to deliver alpha. GPT itself recommends scripted alpha verification (Q5 section 7).

Ranks are 1-6, not 1-8: the Art Bible (section 5.1) fixes the playable cap at rank 6 and the registry holds ranks 1-6. GPT's 8-rank ladders for Cannon, Coil and Bell are not generated; those machines are approved finals and GPT itself warns its ladders must not replace approved identities (Q6 corrections).

The "20-30 FX families" are delivered as 18 six-sprite sheets (108 sprites) built from the effects lab (docs/art/ART_BIBLE.md section 7, art-candidates/fx-lab-v2 README): 12 shoot families, 6 triggers, soft sprites, merge and kill moments.

loop.text: Open a NEW ChatGPT image chat. Paste art-candidates/prompt-pack/primer.txt exactly (copy the file, never retype). Wait for the single word READY. Attach the 2-3 anchors named in the batch, saying which controls what ("Image 1 controls ART STYLE, Image 2 controls CAMERA and MATERIALS. Do not copy their objects.").
Send the batch prompts one at a time, in order, in that chat. Save each raw image untouched as art-candidates/pack-v2/<batch>/raw/<rawFile>. Set status "generated". Never edit a raw file.

Run the slicing pipeline (section 6). Mechanical gates fail fast: wrong size, key not flat, white in holes, cell-edge pixels, duplicate ranks, dull metal, halo. Deterministic failures (stray pixel, key tint) are repaired by script; anything else goes to step 4 as a recorded failure. Status "sliced".
The pipeline writes one review sheet per batch: every cell at 70 px and 110 px on cream #F2E6C9 and charcoal #303139, next to the anchors and the in-game neighbours.

A different reviewer from the generator (a separate agent or the owner) scores every asset with the 20-item rubric plus X1-X6 and returns, per asset: 20 scores, total, critical failures, verdict, and the three lowest criteria with one fix sentence each. A generic "looks good" is invalid. If in doubt: REDO.

REDO and REJECT assets get the FIX template: attach the failed image, send "EDIT THE ATTACHED IMAGE..." with the critic's fix sentences. Two redos at most per asset. After two failed redos stop regenerating the whole sheet: isolate the failing cell, repair it alone, composite by script. A third failure goes to the owner as REJECT with the three attempts attached.

Passed assets are put in the Asset Hub as "draft" with the critic sheet. The owner approves per asset or per batch; only then status "approved" and the file moves to the approved set. Gate A: board + hero + UI kit + monster anchors are judged together at phone size before any other batch starts. Gate B: after units and FX, one home screen and one battle screen are assembled from approved art.

Wiring into src/ is a separate task, started only after the owner has agreed a whole screen or family ("agree on all assets first, wire in later"). Registry status goes placeholder -> draft -> final by hand.

steps.name: Validate input
steps.text: Check the PNG decodes, size equals the prompt canvas (±2%), and the border pixels are flat key colour: median border colour within ΔE 10 of the declared key (#FF00FF, #00FF00 or #000000) and border standard deviation under 6. Otherwise fail "key not flat" (critic repeated this on white backgrounds).

steps.name: Key to alpha
steps.text: Magenta/green key: alpha from the colour distance to the key in Lab, alpha = clamp((ΔE - 14) / (40 - 14)). Black key (additive FX): alpha = max(R,G,B); keep colour unpremultiplied. Backgrounds: no keying.

steps.name: Despill and edge decontamination
steps.text: For every pixel with alpha under 0.98 and within 3 px of the silhouette: estimate the foreground colour as C = (I - (1 - a) * K) / a, then replace the colour of the edge ring by the colour of the nearest interior pixel at least 2 px inside (dilate interior colours outward). Despill only the edge ring: spill = max(0, min(R,B) - G) * 0.9 subtracted from R and B for magenta, the mirror rule for green. Never despill the interior (red, violet and purple parts are legitimate).

steps.name: 1 px erode and feather
steps.text: Erode alpha by 1 px (3x3 cross min filter), then feather alpha only with a Gaussian of sigma 0.6. This kills the pale fringe the critic found on knob, tabs and many UI pieces.

steps.name: Holes
steps.text: Flood-fill the transparent region from the border; any enclosed key-coloured region is also keyed out (shackles, gear centres, handles). Enclosed near-white regions are NOT keyed: they fail gate G3.

steps.name: Sheet segmentation
steps.text: Never crop on fixed grid lines. Dilate the alpha by 12 px, label connected components, expect exactly layout cell-count components (plus the declared empty cells), assign them to cells by centroid, row-major. Count mismatch fails the sheet "layout" (slivers, merged cells and duplicate ranks come from AI grids). Each component is cropped from the undilated alpha.

steps.name: Trim to bbox
steps.text: Crop each object to its alpha bbox (alpha above 8). Single objects, icons, units: pad 8% of the long side, centre on a square canvas. Units: pad 10%. Strips, panels, ribbons, bars: no padding, keep the bbox aspect, and write the 9-slice insets (measured from the uniform border band). FX sprites: pad 10%, centre of brightness at the canvas centre.

steps.name: Export
steps.text: PNG for review, WebP (quality 90, alpha) for shipping. Units and icons 256 px (units 256x256 source, 2x of the 118 px cell), crates 512, FX 256 (rings and glows 512), UI strips at native width up to 1024. Backgrounds: resize cover to 1080x1920, WebP quality 85. Write art-candidates/pack-v2/<batch>/manifest.json with the sha1 of the raw, sizes, gate results and the 9-slice insets.

steps.name: Light and dark checks
steps.text: Composite every cell on cream #F2E6C9, charcoal #303139 and mid blue #3B5BA5 at 70 px and 110 px and write the review sheet. Automatic halo metric: among boundary pixels (alpha 0.05-0.95) the share whose colour differs by more than 25 luminance levels from the nearest interior colour must be at most 2% on both light and dark backgrounds.

gates.name: Dimensions
gates.rule: Raw size equals the canvas in the prompt (±2%); each exported cell is square (single, icon, unit) or within 3% of the requested ratio (strip, panel).

gates.name: Key purity
gates.rule: After S1, key-coloured pixels (within ΔE 20 of the key) inside alpha above 0.5 are at most 0.1% of object pixels, and no pixel with min(R,B) - G above 90 survives on non-magenta objects.

gates.name: White in holes
gates.rule: No enclosed region of near-white (all channels at least 235) with area at least 0.2% of the bbox area. Fails shackles and gear centres filled with white.

gates.name: Cell-edge pixels
gates.rule: No pixel with alpha above 16 within 2 px of the raw cell border; every extra component smaller than 2% of the main object, or touching within 6 px of the cell edge, is a sliver and fails.

gates.name: Occupancy
gates.rule: Single objects: bbox long side 70-90% of the cell (and at least 8% margin each side). Strips and panels: bbox width at least 95% of the stated width. FX: bright mass inside the middle 80%.

gates.name: Stretch uniformity
gates.rule: Panels and strips: border band mean colour per side within 8% of each other; the middle 40% of a strip has a horizontal luminance standard deviation under 4% (so the middle can be stretched); end caps mirror within 10%.

gates.name: Duplicate and monotonic ranks
gates.rule: dHash distance between any two ranks of one unit must be at least 8 (of 64 bits); opaque area must not shrink by more than 3% from one rank to the next. Failures are flagged for the critic, not auto-rejected.

gates.name: Dull metal
gates.rule: Mean saturation of opaque pixels at least 0.30 (the critic measured grey steel at 5-30%); under 0.25 fails. Not applied to FX or cream UI plates.

gates.name: Outline present
gates.rule: At least 80% of the boundary ring (6 px inside the silhouette) has luminance under 0.35 and is not pure black (max channel above 20). Not applied to FX or backgrounds.

gates.name: Additive FX
gates.rule: The four corners of an FX cell are at most 8/255 on every channel; white-only sprites have mean saturation at most 0.15 (tintable); coloured FX are declared in the prompt.

gates.name: Tileable background
gates.rule: For vertical tiles the top and bottom rows match within 6 levels; centre calm: edge density in the middle 40% below the border average.

gates.name: Halo
gates.rule: Boundary halo share at most 2% on cream and charcoal (S8).

noArtNeeded.fx_shake: camera shake only, no sprite needed

statusRule: A status never reaches "critic-pass", "approved" or "wired" while the slicer gate is FAIL or the harsh-critic score is under 18/20. A gate WARN needs a written reason from the critic. The status is copied from docs/art/CRITIQUE_*.md, never set by the generating run ("accepted" by the generator is not a status).

notes.acceptanceRule: Nothing is "accepted" with a slicer gate FAIL or a critic score under 18/20 (CRITIQUE_2 thresholds: PASS 18-20, REDO 14-17, REJECT 1-13). Status comes from the critic file, not from the run that generated the asset.
notes.slicer: tools/slice-sheet.mjs trims every cell to the object box before padding. Gate fill: strips fail when the object is under 90 percent of the output width, every other kind when its larger side is under 70 percent of the canvas. Gate minHeight: a strip fails when the object is under 24 px tall at 1x. Strips are written at 1024 px (PNG, 2x) and 512 px (WebP, 1x). Key green is supported (--key green).
